newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian airforce plane with three crew crashes.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian airforce plane with three crew crashes.

text.p: A Nigerian airforce plane crashed near the northern city of Kaduna on Monday night, an official statement said on Tuesday without giving details of casualties.

It said the Dornier 128-6 Sky Servant, enroute to the capital Abuja and with two pilots and a technician on board, crashed some three km (two miles) from the military airport in Kaduna while making its approach to land.
"The fate of the persons on board will be made known after contact with their families," said one air force officer, adding that there were no passengers aboard the plane.

No reason was given for the cause of the crash but aviation sources said it could have been visibility, usually poor in northern Nigeria at this time of the year because of harmattan winds blowing southwards from the arid north.
It is the second air crash within two months in Nigeria, which has a poor air safety record.
Last month poor visibility caused a light aircraft to crash on landing in the northeastern town of Yola, killing five people.
In November a plane on a domestic flight crashed into a lagoon near Lagos killing all 143 on board.
